article.intro: Need a name for whoever's just walked into the tavern? This **D&D fantasy name generator** gives you a first and family name for any of the common races, each in that race's own naming style, or a whole random party at once: a dwarf, a tiefling, a halfling and a dragonborn, with their races beside their names.

sections.heading: Each race names itself differently
sections.content:
• Humans in the Forgotten Realms have regional styles, like Chondathan and Illuskan, much as real countries do.
  • Elves have a family name that translates into Common, and only take an adult name after about a century.
  • Dwarves carry a clan name and guard their family's honour fiercely.
  • Halflings and gnomes are fond of nicknames; gnomes can have half a dozen names.
  • Dragonborn give their clan name first, before their own.
  • Tieflings often have infernal names, or take a virtue as a name instead.

The generator follows each race's pattern, so a dragonborn comes out clan first.

sections.heading: Names for NPCs on the fly
sections.content:
• Generate a batch before the session. Keep a list of names by race so you never have to stop and think when a player asks the innkeeper's name.
  • Use "Any race" for crowds. A random party is perfect for a rival adventuring group, a tavern full of strangers or a caravan.
  • Cross out the ones you use, and write a word beside each: "nervous", "owes money". That's an NPC.

sections.heading: More names for each race
sections.content:
Each race has its own page with more options and the story behind its names: Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, Gnome, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Tiefling and Dragonborn. The D&D names hub has everything else, from taverns to goblins.

Need someone the party wasn't supposed to talk to? The NPC Name Generator adds a job and a quirk to every name.

faqs.question: What races does it cover?
faqs.answer: Human, elf, dwarf, halfling, gnome, half-elf, half-orc, tiefling and dragonborn, the common races of D&D. Choose "Any race" for a random mix.

faqs.question: Are these the names from the Player's Handbook?
faqs.answer: No. They're new names in each race's style, drawn from this site's race generators, so your characters won't share a name with the book's examples.

faqs.question: Can I use these names in my campaign?
faqs.answer: Yes, they're free to use and you don't need to credit the site.
